problem:
The displacement $s,$ in meters, relative to a fixed origin $O$ of a particle moving in a straight line along the $x$-axis is given by 
$s(t)=(4t-12)^{2},$
where $t\ge 0$ is the time measured in seconds. Determine the time intervals in which the particle is moving in the direction of decreasing $x.$

$t\in [${{field-1}},

{{field-2}}$)$
worked_solution:
If the particle moves in the direction of decreasing $x,$ then its velocity is negative.

First, we calculate the velocity function by differentiating the position function:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\frac{\text{d}s}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}\,((4t-12)^{2}) \\  & =8(4t-12) \\  & =32(t-3)\end{aligned}
$$

To calculate time intervals in which the particle is moving in the direction of decreasing $x,$ we solve the inequality $v(t)<0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & <0 \\ 32(t-3) & <0 \\ t-3 & <0 \\ t & <3\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the time interval in which the particle is moving in the direction of decreasing $x$ is

$$
t\in [0,\,3).
$$
